requirements.quote:
Inverse queries take the form of a single RR in the answer section of
the message, with an empty question section.
requirements.required_behavior: Place exactly one resource record in the answer section.
requirements.why_checkable: The answer-section record count and record placement can be inspected in an encoded inverse query.

requirements.quote:
Inverse queries take the form of a single RR in the answer section of
the message, with an empty question section.
requirements.why_checkable: The inverse-query question section can be parsed to verify that it contains no questions.

requirements.quote:
The owner name of the
query RR and its TTL are not significant.
requirements.condition: When matching the resource record supplied in an inverse query.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use the owner name of the query resource record as a significant matching criterion.
requirements.why_checkable: Queries differing only in the query RR owner name can be compared to verify that the name does not affect resource matching.

requirements.quote:
The owner name of the
query RR and its TTL are not significant.
requirements.condition: When matching the resource record supplied in an inverse query.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use the TTL of the query resource record as a significant matching criterion.
requirements.why_checkable: Queries differing only in the query RR TTL can be compared to verify that the TTL does not affect resource matching.

requirements.quote:
Inverse queries take the form of a single RR in the answer section of
the message, with an empty question section.  The owner name of the
query RR and its TTL are not significant.  The response carries
questions in the question section which identify all names possessing
the query RR WHICH THE NAME SERVER KNOWS.
requirements.condition: When returning matching names in an inverse-query response.
requirements.required_behavior: Include every name known to the responding name server that possesses the queried resource record.
requirements.why_checkable: A server with a controlled set of matching names can be queried and the returned name set compared with all known matches.

requirements.quote:
Since no name server knows
about all of the domain name space, the response can never be assumed to
be complete.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Assume that the returned names are the complete set throughout the domain name space.
requirements.why_checkable: Response consumers can be inspected for an inference that unreturned names cannot possess the queried resource.

requirements.quote:
Inverse queries are NOT an
acceptable method of mapping host addresses to host names; use the IN-
ADDR.ARPA domain instead.
requirements.condition: When mapping host addresses to host names.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use inverse queries as the method of address-to-host-name mapping.
requirements.why_checkable: The address-to-host-name resolution path can be inspected to determine whether it issues inverse queries.

requirements.quote:
Inverse queries are NOT an
acceptable method of mapping host addresses to host names; use the IN-
ADDR.ARPA domain instead.
requirements.condition: When mapping host addresses to host names.
requirements.why_checkable: The address-to-host-name resolution path can be inspected for use of the IN-ADDR.ARPA namespace.

requirements.quote:
Where possible, name servers should provide case-insensitive comparisons
for inverse queries.  Thus an inverse query asking for an MX RR of
"Venera.isi.edu" should get the same response as a query for
"VENERA.ISI.EDU"; an inverse query for HINFO RR "IBM-PC UNIX" should
produce the same result as an inverse query for "IBM-pc unix".  However,
this cannot be guaranteed because name servers may possess RRs that
contain character strings but the name server does not know that the
data is character.
requirements.condition: When processing inverse queries and case-insensitive comparison is possible; this is advisory and is not guaranteed for character data whose character nature the name server does not know.
requirements.required_behavior: The name server should provide case-insensitive comparisons.
requirements.why_checkable: For resource formats recognized as character data, queries differing only in letter case can be compared; the stated feasibility limitation and advisory strength remain part of the check.

requirements.quote:
When a name server processes an inverse query, it either returns:

   1. zero, one, or multiple domain names for the specified
      resource as QNAMEs in the question section



Mockapetris                                                    [Page 40]


RFC 1035        Domain Implementation and Specification    November 1987


   2. an error code indicating that the name server doesn't support
      inverse mapping of the specified resource type.
requirements.condition: When a name server processes an inverse query and returns names rather than an unsupported-type error.
requirements.required_behavior: Return zero, one, or multiple domain names for the specified resource as QNAMEs in the question section.
requirements.why_checkable: Inverse-query responses can be parsed to verify the placement and QNAME representation of returned domain names, including an empty result.

requirements.quote:
When a name server processes an inverse query, it either returns:

   1. zero, one, or multiple domain names for the specified
      resource as QNAMEs in the question section



Mockapetris                                                    [Page 40]


RFC 1035        Domain Implementation and Specification    November 1987


   2. an error code indicating that the name server doesn't support
      inverse mapping of the specified resource type.
requirements.condition: When a name server processes an inverse query for a resource type whose inverse mapping it does not support.
requirements.error_behavior: Return an error code indicating that inverse mapping of the specified resource type is unsupported.
requirements.why_checkable: An inverse query for an unsupported resource type can verify that the response reports unsupported inverse mapping without inventing a particular numeric error code.

requirements.quote:
When the response to an inverse query contains one or more QNAMEs, the
owner name and TTL of the RR in the answer section which defines the
inverse query is modified to exactly match an RR found at the first
QNAME.
requirements.condition: When an inverse-query response contains one or more QNAMEs.
requirements.required_behavior: Modify the owner name of the answer-section resource record defining the inverse query to exactly match an RR found at the first QNAME.
requirements.why_checkable: The response RR owner name can be compared against the matching RR at the first returned QNAME.

requirements.quote:
When the response to an inverse query contains one or more QNAMEs, the
owner name and TTL of the RR in the answer section which defines the
inverse query is modified to exactly match an RR found at the first
QNAME.
requirements.condition: When an inverse-query response contains one or more QNAMEs.
requirements.required_behavior: Modify the TTL of the answer-section resource record defining the inverse query to exactly match the same RR found at the first QNAME.
requirements.why_checkable: The response RR TTL can be compared against the matching RR at the first returned QNAME, ensuring the rewritten owner name and TTL describe the same RR.

requirements.quote:
RRs returned in the inverse queries cannot be cached using the same
mechanism as is used for the replies to standard queries.
requirements.condition: When caching resource records returned in inverse-query responses.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Cache those resource records using the same mechanism used for replies to standard queries.
requirements.why_checkable: The cache insertion path for inverse-query RRs can be checked for inappropriate reuse of standard-query reply caching.
